# Ezekiel 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-the-word-of YHWH came to-me, saying:

**2** "Son-of man, what is the-wood-of the-vine more-than any wood, the-vine-branch which is among-the-trees-of the-forest?

**3** Is wood taken from-it to-make into-any work? Or-do-they-take from-it a-peg to-hang upon-it any vessel?

**4** Behold, to-the-fire it-is-given for-fuel; its-two ends the-fire has-consumed, and-its-middle is-charred — is-it-useful for-any work?

**5** Behold, when-it-was whole it-was-not-made into-any work; how-much-less when the-fire has-consumed-it and-it-is-charred — can-it-still-be-made into-any work?

**6** Therefore thus says the-Lord YHWH: 'As the-wood-of the-vine among the-trees-of the-forest which I-have-given to-the-fire for-fuel, so I-have-given the-inhabitants-of Jerusalem.

**7** And-I-will-set My-face against-them; from-the-fire they-went-out, and-the-fire shall-consume-them; and-you-shall-know that I [am] YHWH when-I-set My-face against-them.

**8** And-I-will-make the-land a-desolation because they-acted unfaithfully,'" declares the-Lord YHWH.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **15:2**: Mah-yihyeh etz ha-gefen — 'what is the wood of the vine?' The vine metaphor (Israel as God's vine, cf. Isa 5, Ps 80) is inverted: vine-wood is useless for construction. Israel's only value was fruitfulness; without it, she's fuel.

- **15:4**: Both ends burned, middle charred — likely referring to the deportations of 605 and 597 BCE. The remnant in Jerusalem is already partially consumed.

- **15:6**: The shortest allegory in Ezekiel, yet devastating in its logic: the vine's only purpose is bearing fruit. Strip that away, and vine-wood is inferior to every other wood.

— EMET
